doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Studio work with Jarre, Farnon, Mancini, Oscar Peterson and Mel Torme
summary: Appleyard lists studio sessions and recalls touring and recording with Mel Torme.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Amazing. You mentioned doing some studio work over the years. Do you have any particular things that you remember from your studio work, either wonderful or ridiculous?

I recorded for Maurice Jarre, who did Dr. Zhivago and all those films. I recorded for the greatest vocal writer that ever lived, Robert Farnon. I did his “Porgy & Bess.” I did, for Oscar Peterson, “The Canadiana Suite,” that was a highlight as a percussionist. I did Henry Mancini. I remember Mancini coming over to me and said, “No, I don’t want it played — I want it done like this” and he picked up the mallets. And then I did — I
recorded with Anne Murray, Gordon Lightfoot, oh gosh, I can’t remember them all. I recorded with Mel Torme — Mel Torment as Buddy Rich used to call him.

Yeah. I traveled with him too, to Japan, and played Michael’s Pub with him for a month in New York. And we recorded in Tokyo. That was a great experience working with him. He wasn’t that generous with the money but musically it was most gratifying. I enjoyed that.
